text:
ashley: quick check — running into 401s when using the Node/TS SDK inside Vite dev SSR and Next edge functions. Authorization header seems to be missing on requests that the SDK issues. anyone seen this? repro: sdk@1.4.0, project is ESM (package.json type: "module"), vite dev + next edge runtime.

noah: hmm. have you checked whether the bundler replaced global fetch or mutated headers? vite sometimes injects a light fetch shim in dev that behaves slightly different.

ashley: yeah i suspected that. in network tab the outbound call is missing Authorization. the SDK logs the token is present before calling fetch. so the header is lost during bundling/runtime, not when building the request.

taylor: two common things i've seen: 1) bundlers picking the CJS build which uses a different global shim; 2) ssr/dev polyfills replacing fetch with a non-spec one that drops headers. for vite try ssr.noExternal or optimizeDeps.exclude for the sdk package so the runtime uses the authored ESM. eg:
```js
// vite.config.js
export default defineConfig({
  ssr: {
    noExternal: ['@redwood/inference']
  },
})
```
or for next (app dir) use next.config.js transpilePackages: ['@redwood/inference']

ashley: ok i'll try noExternal. question: why would CJS vs ESM affect header behavior?

noah: if the bundler resolves to the CJS entry, sometimes the package expects a Node global env and uses a small fetch wrapper that sets headers differently. ESM dist tends to include code paths compatible with edge globals (globalThis.fetch). essentially different entrypoints -> different runtime assumptions.

jen: also double-check your vite dev server isn't using a proxy that strips auth. but that usually shows up earlier.

ashley: i tried ssr.noExternal + restarted vite and the auth header now shows up in the outbound request. nice. streaming still flaky in the edge function though — partial streams drop after first chunk sometimes.

taylor: streaming + dev server is rough. vite's transforms for streaming responses (and some middlewares) can consume the body. for Next edge functions make sure you run on the actual edge runtime (not `next dev` server) to reproduce — dev mode can mutate streaming. for local debugging you can set NODE_OPTIONS="--no-experimental-fetch-polyfill"? ymmv.

ashley: noted. any permanent packaging fixes we should do on the SDK side so customers don't hit this?

noah: a few suggestions for the SDK package:
- ensure package.json exports map provides clear esm/cjs entries and avoids defaulting to CJS for bundlers that prefer require-style resolution.
- ship a small shim that detects broken fetch shims and falls back to constructing a Request with Headers explicitly (defensive header copying).
- document common bundler configs (vite ssr.noExternal, next transpilePackages) in the quickstart.

jen: +1 for a short section in getting-started about dev-mode pitfalls (vite dev, next dev) and a one-liner for the workaround.

ashley: i'll open a tiny PR adding a note to docs and an example vite.config snippet. also will add a repro app in devex/sdks repo.

ci-bot: build passed for branch fix/docs-vite-auth-workaround (CI run 4821) :white_check_mark:

taylor: for long term we could add a runtime check in the SDK that logs a warning when Authorization header is dropped (detect by making a preflight no-op or checking header mutation hooks). less ideal but would save time.

ashley: thanks all — PR incoming. saved me a bunch. :thumbsup:

noah: nice! fyi i also ran into an ESM/CJS sourcemap oddity when using older node versions — might be worth calling out minimum node version in the docs too.

ashley: good call. i'll add node >= 18 note and the vite/next tips.

jen: cheers — ping us when the doc PR is up and i'll loop in docs-review. :sparkles:
